title: git fetch
definition: Downloads commits, files, and refs from a remote repository into your local repo, but does NOT merge those changes into your working directory.
simpleExplanation: The safe way to see what your team has been working on. It downloads all their new code from GitHub into your local `.git` hidden folder, but it explicitly DOES NOT touch the code you are currently looking at in VS Code. You can review their code safely before merging it.
realWorldExample: Checking if anyone pushed changes to the `main` branch over the weekend without actually risking breaking the code you are currently writing.

basic: Does `git fetch` overwrite the files in your Working Directory?
intermediate: How do you view the changes you just fetched?

answers.question: Overwrite files?
answers.answer: No. Never. That is the entire point of `fetch`. It is completely safe.

answers.question: View changes?
answers.answer: You can use `git log origin/main` to see the newly downloaded commits, or `git diff main origin/main` to see the exact code differences.

codeExample:
# Download all new data from the 'origin' server
$ git fetch origin

# Look at what your coworkers pushed to the 'main' branch on the server
$ git log origin/main

# Compare your local 'main' branch with the server's 'main' branch
$ git diff main origin/main

# If you like their changes, you manually merge them in!
$ git merge origin/main
